title.narrative: Support for Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria

description.narrative: With the Syria crisis in its thirteenth year, the humanitarian crisis has been exacerbated by the widespread presence of explosive ordnance in areas populated by civilians; including improvised explosive devices, landmines, and other explosive remnants of war. While the full scale of contamination is not precisely known, according to the 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview, more than 65% of the Syrian population (14.4 million people) are at risk from explosive ordnance contamination, which represents over 20% increase from 2023.\n\nUNOPS supports UNMAS in its humanitarian mine action intervention to mitigate the risk of explosive ordnance for communities and humanitarian workers in the UN hubs, through coordination, risk education and non-technical survey in Syria.
